title: Renal Function Trend After Contrast Study
scenario: A 70-year-old male client with diabetes and hypertension received IV contrast for a CT angiogram. The nurse monitors serial renal function labs and urine output over the following three days.

questions.subject: Medical-Surgical
questions.stem: Reviewing the three-day trend, which interpretation is most accurate?

options.text: The rising creatinine and BUN with falling urine output indicate worsening acute kidney injury
The renal function is stable and within expected limits
The findings reflect improving kidney function
The changes are due to dehydration and require no follow-up

questions.rationale: Creatinine climbing from 1.1 to 2.6, BUN from 18 to 40, and urine output dropping to 22 mL/hr over three days after contrast exposure indicate contrast-induced acute kidney injury that is worsening, not resolving.

questions.subject: Medical-Surgical
questions.stem: Based on the Day 3 trend, which nursing actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.

options.text: Notify the provider of the declining renal function
Monitor the client for signs of hyperkalemia
Review the medication list for nephrotoxic drugs
Continue strict intake and output monitoring

questions.rationale: Worsening AKI with a potassium of 5.4 warrants provider notification, hyperkalemia monitoring, nephrotoxin review, and continued I&O tracking. A high-potassium diet would worsen hyperkalemia, and withholding all fluids is not indicated.
